notes: The player serves a hostile table alone, cut off from the servants' hall after defying the Major in the study, and is pressed twice for the hour: once in a whisper from Miss Gresham at the sideboard, once aloud by the Major with his watch on the cloth. The nephew's bolt for the stables lands mid-scene and locks the house tighter; the sherry glass in the pantry is the one quiet clue, and the service door is the way on.
opening: Dinner on the second night of the snow, and the master's chair stands empty at the head of the cloth with his place laid as if he might come down. No maid has come up to carry for you: since you answered the Major back in the study doorway with your keys in your fist, Fairbrother has seen to it that the servants' hall sends up its dishes and nothing else, and you serve the table alone from the sideboard. Major Carrington has his gold watch open on the linen beside the empty place and is telling Miss Davenport, loudly enough for the house, that the quarrel was at eleven by it and that he will carry the household's account to the magistrate at the thaw. Mr. Yardley sits white over an untouched plate, and Miss Gresham, who has risen to help with the tureen as no lady should, stands at your elbow with her back to them all.

variants.text: The Major's eye finds you each time you pass behind his chair, and stays. He has moved the carving set to his own side of the cloth, where you would have to reach past him for it.
The watch is gone from the cloth. Sleet rattles the north windows and the grate has burned down to a red line nobody has asked you to mend.

The master's chair is empty at the head of the cloth, his place laid, his portrait above the grate looking down the length of the table at the four who are left. The north windows are black and the sleet comes against them in handfuls.
The tray has been stacked and left for you alone; the glass cloths are folded with a valet's precision and not one maid has been near. Fairbrother's message is the empty room.
The plate-warmer ticks as it cools. The lead sink holds one sherry glass, washed and set upside down, that was not among the dinner things you sent up.

options.detail: 'The master kept his settlements at ten.'
options.label: 'Settlements at ten.' carry it round
options.text: You take the weight of the dish and say it low, for her alone: the master kept his settlements at ten, miss, everybody knew it. Her fingers come off the handles. You carry the soup round the table and the table hears nothing but soup; the word she was shaping is never said.

options.detail: 'What did you beg him for, miss?'
options.label: 'What did you beg him for, miss?'
options.text: You lean in over the tureen and ask her outright what she begged the master for at ten. Her face goes to paper. At that moment the yard door bangs and Mr. Yardley is dragged in half-frozen between the groom and Fairbrother, and the first thing he sees is his intended bent to a servant's ear with her back to the room.

options.label: carry the tureen to the Major first
options.text: You lift the dish from her hands without meeting her eye and go to the Major's place first, as the order of the table requires. Her lips close on whatever they had shaped. The ladle rings once against the rim and she sits down.

lapse.text: Miss Gresham sets the tureen down on the sideboard herself, badly, and goes back to her chair with the question unasked and unanswered.

options.label: set the next course down, say nothing
options.text: You set the dish down beside the open watch and say nothing. The Major closes it with a snap and tells the table that here is a sensible woman who keeps to her plate. Miss Davenport finishes her eleven without a tremor.

options.detail: 'The hall clock struck half past ten, sir.'
options.label: 'The hall clock struck half past ten.'
options.text: You say it to the cloth, not to him: the hall clock struck the half hour through the study door while the voices were still raised, and it was half past ten. Miss Davenport's recital stops in the middle of a word. The Major's hand closes over the watch and stays closed.

options.label: set the hall clock against his watch
options.text: You ask the table's leave and do not wait for it. The long-case clock in the hall stands silent in the cold: Fairbrother has stopped the pendulum for the dead, and the hands are fixed at the hour the body was found this morning. You come back with the chill of the hall on you and nothing in your hands, and the Major is already watching the door. 'The house keeps the hours Fairbrother keeps,' he says.

options.detail: 'The hour is the magistrate's to fix, sir.'
options.label: 'That's for the magistrate, sir.'
options.text: You say the hour is for the magistrate to fix and not for the housekeeper, and pour his wine. He lets it pass. The watch stays open on the cloth, its chain across the master's plate.

lapse.text: The Major pockets the watch without having had your word, and tells Miss Davenport that the servants will say what the servants are told.

actions.label: the sherry glass from the sink
actions.text: The glass has been washed by someone who did not wash glasses for a living: a crust of sherry still dried in the foot. On the underside of the rim, where a thumb would not find it, is a single bead of white wax. White wax, in a house where the study candlestick now holds a yellow tallow stub.

actions.label: out through the service door
actions.text: With the nephew locked in and Fairbrother set at his door, there is nobody left to send you anywhere. You stack the tray, take up your keys, and go through the service door into the cold of the back passage; behind you the Major's chair scrapes as he rises to see which way you went.

events.text: The Major sets down his glass and tells the table that the quarrel in the study is known to all of them, and that he will carry the household's account to the magistrate at the thaw, name by name and hour by hour. Mr. Yardley kicks his chair over backwards and is out through the yard door into the storm before anyone has risen. The groom and Fairbrother bring him back a quarter of an hour later, white to the lips and his coat stiff with ice, and he is taken up and locked in his room with the valet set on a chair outside it. The chair stays on its back on the carpet.

nudges.text: The Major's voice, pitched to carry through any door in this house: 'The housekeeper will account for her rounds when she has done hiding behind the soup.'
Somewhere above, a door is tried from the inside and found locked, and Fairbrother's chair creaks as he settles against it.

props.name: the Major's watch
props.description: A gold hunter, open on the white cloth with its chain laid across the master's empty place. Its hands say ten past eight. It is the only clock in the house the Major has not let anyone else wind.
